comments.text: Read-only check at 11:35 UTC, 13 min after the reboot; the user is on the Mac, so nothing was changed. (1) The wallpaper is ALREADY STATIC: Index.plist provider com.apple.wallpaper.choice.image = Solid Colors/Gold 2.png. No aerial process is running, and WallpaperAgent and WallpaperImageExtension are at 0%. The idle screen saver is still an aerial (provider .screen-saver), which only matters when it starts. (2) colorsync is still busy WITHOUT any video wallpaper: colorsyncd + colorsync.displayservices sampled 1/s for 20 s gave 12 29 74 1 6 47 35 42 3 56 15 39 2 56 11 48 1 78 6 51 % (bursty, mean ~33% of one core; before the reboot it was ~100%). So the wallpaper was not the driver. The bursts look like display-profile work, i.e. virtual displays being configured or captured (pinpin-displays, atlas, sunshine): a question for whoever owns displays and atlas, not a wallpaper fix. Proposal: close K21 as done by the user. If colorsync keeps hurting air_smoke, open a card to correlate its bursts with pinpin-displays and atlas events (read-only log show). air_smoke not re-run: it needs EXCLUSIVE, and the laptop is read-only for now.

cards.title: colorsync CPU on the Air: which display/event drives it
cards.details: 30-min read-only correlation of colorsyncd + colorsync.displayservices CPU against the pinpin-displays log, atlas capture restarts and per-display config (scale, HDR, profile); find the driver and propose a fix; then air_smoke under the exclusive lock in a gap of work-34's campaign. Follows K21 (wallpaper ruled out).

comments.text:
FINDINGS (30 min read-only, 11:27–11:57 UTC; data: Air ~/.local/share/pinpin-apps/colorsync-study-20261104T112707Z).
- colorsyncd + displayservices averaged 38% of a core (p90 58%) and GREW over the 30 min: displayservices 19.7 -> 28.2%, colorsyncd 11.9 -> 17.1%. No other process grew.
- The work is XPC display-info requests; each one rebuilds the profiles of all 7 displays. The rate went from 92/min to 203/min (4428 in total).
- DRIVER: virtual-display churn. The rate steps up whenever a virtual display is created and removed, and never comes back down:
  - 11:29 display 10: +15/min
  - 11:39 display 11: +11/min
  - 11:43 display 11 removed: 140 -> 156
  - 11:51 display 12: +12/min
  - 11:55 display 13: +18/min
  Each one was pinpin-displays 'screen 63 -> display N (1600x1000 @1x)', living 12 s to 4 min.
- Not the driver: the 29 atlas restarts (a step of about 0), the per-display config (all sRGB, 60 Hz, no HDR, no profile changes), or the wallpaper.
- Extrapolation: about +100 req/min and +13 CPU points per half hour at this churn, reaching a full core after hours of uptime. That matches the ~100% before the reboot.

WHO MAKES SCREEN 63: unknown. It isn't stress.py (synth now; sck uses ids 2–11), eval_run.sh (60) or the apps tests (47). PinPin Host closes a status-bar window at the same moments, so it's probably something Host- or headset-driven.
PROPOSED FIX:
A) No churn. Create virtual displays once from a fixed pool of scratch ids and never remove them per run; tests reuse them (60, 47, 63...). The macOS display ids stop counting up.
B) Mitigation until then. Restart colorsync.displayservices when it stays above ~40% for 10 min. It's in the system launchd domain, so this needs root (a privileged helper in PinPin Host); launchd relaunches it with fresh state. Test it once under an exclusive lock.
C) Visibility. A colorsync line on /status (CPU and requests/min), red above 40%, so the creep shows before air_smoke fails. I can do C now.
